recommendations.title: Review recent high-severity anomalies
recommendations.explanation: 2 high-severity event(s) in the last 30 days. Most severe: unusually low use around Sun 2017-12-17 04:00: 846.03 kW vs typical 1264.16 kW for this hour of the week, 2.4x the edge of the usual range for this hour (the 99.5th-percentile deviation of the last 26 weeks). Event spans 2 h. Largest contributor: FOX-B04, 160 kWh below its own expected load over the event (25% of the summed building deviations).
caveats: An anomaly is an unusual reading relative to the weekly pattern, not a confirmed fault; term breaks and events are flagged too.

recommendations.title: Review what keeps the minimum demand high
recommendations.explanation: The lowest sustained demand is about 1,068 kW (the 5th percentile of hourly demand), which is 74% of all energy used in the last 89 days. Lighting, ventilation, pumps and standby equipment in shared areas are common contributors; the meter data cannot say which are present here.

scenario.assumption: each 10% reduction of the minimum demand

caveats: Figures are scenario estimates under the stated assumption, not forecasts of savings.
The tariff in use is the built-in DEMO tariff; replace it with your real rates before relying on any cost figure.
The base load is a statistical floor of the whole-society reading, not a measurement of individual devices.

recommendations.title: FOX-B10 uses 6.2x the median energy per square metre
recommendations.explanation: In the last 89 days FOX-B10 used 127.4 kWh per m2 against a median of 20.5 kWh per m2 across the society's buildings. Differences in occupancy, equipment or building age can explain part of this; an energy audit of the building is the way to find out.

scenario.assumption: arithmetic comparison only: the building at the median intensity

caveats: A comparison with peers, not a measured saving; occupancy and use are not in the data.

recommendations.title: Daily demand peaks most often around 18:00
recommendations.explanation: On 31% of days the highest hourly demand falls in the hour starting 18:00. The average daily peak is 1,638 kW against an average demand of 1,439 kW (peak-to-average 1.14). If the utility charges for peak demand, flattening this peak is where the value is; this tariff model has no demand charge.
caveats: Hourly averages hide shorter peaks; an instantaneous peak can be higher.
